summary:
Beyond Earth — Project Summary

Beyond Earth is a child-friendly browser game about exploring a fictional Mars outpost and preparing for a return mission. Players guide Rami through a persistent world while Sami offers optional, contextual advice. A skippable, replayable five-panel comic introduces the story.

Across four seasonal chapters, players scan locations, solve science-themed puzzles, mine and collect resources, manage limited carrying and storage, process water, build and maintain facilities, grow crops, assemble a rocket, and complete a return mission. Progress is saved locally in the browser.

The game uses curated NASA and Canadian Space Agency references to encourage evidence-based thinking. Science notes are bundled offline; the game does not call NASA/CSA APIs during play. Observations, interpretations, and invented gameplay rules are kept distinct. Resource quantities, crop yields, hazards, and engineering outcomes are fictional game mechanics—not measurements, forecasts, or validated Mars-system designs.

Built with JavaScript, Phaser 3, and Vite, the prototype needs no game server, database, private API key, or runtime generative AI. It claims no NASA/CSA endorsement, and learning impact has not yet been measured. The team should confirm its selected challenge and submission details before entering.
details:
Beyond Earth is a browser STEM game for ages 7–12, set on a fictional Mars outpost. Players guide Rami and scripted-AI companion Sami across four seasons: scan, solve evidence puzzles, mine and carry resources, purify water, build a shielded habitat, grow crops, and fuel and assemble a return rocket. A five-panel comic opens the mission; contextual dialogue and a science library explain it.

NASA/CSA references support hands-on learning in source literacy, resource cycles, trade-offs and systems thinking. The intended impact is curiosity, not an asserted learning gain. Citations separate observations from fictional locations, yields, costs, hazards and rocket operations; gameplay is not a Mars forecast or validated engineering. Curated science records are local; gameplay calls no live NASA/CSA APIs.

Built with JavaScript, Phaser 3, Vite, HTML Canvas, CSS, JSON and browser storage, it supports mobile and offline play after caching. No special hardware is needed. Manus AI assisted with code, research, documentation and art. The team reports Canvas (prototypes); Leonardo.AI, Bing, Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT (brainstorming); Claude (asset prompts); ARTcraft (graphic design/editing); Copilot (frontend); Gemini Nano v3 (assets/images). Product variants, versions, rights and asset mapping need confirmation. Design priorities include an illustrated prologue, child-friendly language, accessibility and transparent science boundaries.
